To this day I love to talk religion with people and regularly get into religious discussions with believers who enjoy a respectful conversation. I don't try to convert anyone and generally head off attempts to convert me with the disclaimer that it's futile. I don't think I've ever had an argument or other negative experience about religion. I don't get the taboo on discussing it, really.

It taught me critical thinking. I was devoutly religious as a young child, but argument by argument I strayed towards the Atheistic man typing this comment. Particularly the Atheist community on YouTube was a big influence, and it also got me interested in how I could've been so wrong about something I was so sure of. That led me to learn about logical fallacies, syllogisms, and eventually to philosophy in general, then science - I ended up studying physics at Uni.
